title: Portia Import Proposal
description: Version-1 immutable import-staging proposal produced from one exact Import Source Record under its exact Import Batch mapping profile. It maps source-side assertions toward one possible Portia target without creating a canonical record, establishing person identity, or converting source-system labels into Portia judgments.
$comment: One Import Source Record may yield zero, one, or many Import Proposals. proposal_key is stable only within the exact mapping profile and source record; proposal_identity_digest is application-recomputed from the exact source record identity, exact batch mapping identity, proposal_key, target, and field bindings. Source values are referenced rather than copied when possible. transformed_candidate is allowed only when the exact mapping deterministically produces a value that is not byte/value-identical to the source field. human_resolution_required supplies no value.

x-portia-application-invariants.description: import_batch_id and source_record_id must resolve one exact Import Source Record in the same class and exact Import Batch. Mapping profile/version/digest are inherited only from that exact batch.

A source record may produce zero, one, or many proposals. proposal_key must be deterministic and unique for logical proposals produced by the exact mapping profile; list position, source row order, and local proposal_id are not logical identity inputs.

proposal_identity_digest must be recomputed from a versioned canonical encoding of exact source-record identity, exact batch import/mapping identity, proposal_key, target, and field bindings. Unchanged replay must reconcile the same logical proposal rather than duplicate it.

source_value bindings reference the exact source field and do not copy its value into the proposal. transformed_candidate is stored only when deterministic mapping actually produces a distinct candidate needed for review.
A transformed_candidate is a mapping candidate only. Normalization, parsing, code translation, or format conversion does not establish truth, authority, identity, judgment, or canonical acceptance.

human_resolution_required identifies a target field that cannot be safely resolved automatically. It supplies no implied null/false/no value and must be resolved or left unresolved by attributable review.

Mapping must not use similar name/email, row position, nearby labels, or fuzzy matching to silently create or merge Actor, roster-student, participant, or other person identity. Ambiguity requires human review.

Source labels must not automatically become Portia Classification, Hypothesis, Determination, fault, severity, Response appropriateness, Support recommendation, Fidelity, Outcome, recurrence failure, Reentry completion, or Repair meaning.
new_work target context is allowed only for Event or Support Process roots. Child records require exact existing work context or another explicitly valid target relationship during materialization.
existing_work and existing_record contexts are exact historical references and must not silently follow successor, correction, migration, consolidation, or ownership correction.

Persisting an Import Proposal never creates or changes a canonical Portia record. Human review is required wherever the target family, mapping ambiguity, identity resolution, or local policy requires it.
A later reviewed canonical record uses creation_source.type import. Import provenance does not establish source-system authority, authenticity, accuracy, or truth.
Import Proposal must not carry route_id, Page Record, Page Target, retained-source, OCR/mark interpretation, or paper_capture provenance.

A later mapping profile/version may create a different proposal generation/identity, but earlier source records, proposals, reviews, and canonical records remain preserved and are not silently rewritten.
